session.assistantText:
Your goal is that a single executor keeps walking the whole repo and summarizing it line by line, round after round, on its own, until you call a halt. The repo is 80 placeholder data files plus a README, so the deliverable is a per-round summary tree under `summaries/round-NNN/` with one short line per source line.

What I set up, since you asked me not to do the sweep myself:

- The executor is a running subagent (`poteto-agent` on `magpie/workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash` at low effort, the routine role for this job). It loops rounds on its own inside one turn.
- `scripts/check-round.sh N` is the checkable predicate for a round. It fails if any of the 80 data files lacks a non-empty summary or if `INDEX.md` is missing.
- `scripts/list-rounds.sh` shows how many rounds exist and how many files each one covers.
- The repo is now on a baseline commit, and the executor commits each verified round separately so the sequence reads as an argument.
- A goal is armed for automatic continuation, so the run keeps going across turns until you say stop.

I will report the round count, final check state, and commit SHAs when the executor reports back. If you want it stopped, say so and I will kill the child and pause the goal.

--- turn 2 ---

The executor is stopped and the automatic-continuation goal is paused, so nothing will restart on its own.

**Where it stopped.** It produced zero complete rounds. `summaries/` is empty, `decisions.tsv` was never created, and the only commit is the baseline `c8708be` I made before spawning it. The interrupt landed while it was still on round 1, before the first verification passed. There is nothing partial to salvage, and no data file was modified.

**Why it went nowhere.** My brief asked for "as many rounds as you can within your turn budget", so it was going to grind rounds inside one long turn with no external checkpoint. That is the wrong shape. A subagent that loops indefinitely inside a single turn has no place to report progress, no cheap way to check its own drift, and it burns the whole budget on repetition. The check script existed, but nothing forced the executor to stop and let the parent look between rounds.

**What I would change next.** Two options, and the second is what I recommend.

- Bounded rounds per turn. Tell the executor "do exactly three rounds, then stop and report", and drive the next batch from the parent. Every three rounds the parent reads the check output and the git log, so a drift or a broken round gets caught in minutes instead of after the whole sweep.
- A target instead of a sweep. If the point is coverage rather than repetition, then one round over all 81 files plus a re-verification pass is the whole job. Rounds 2 through N re-summarize identical placeholder lines and produce no new information.

Say the word and I will run the three-rounds-at-a-time version, or the single coverage pass.
